title: Seven tea estates in Keralam’s Vandiperiyar announce lockout

ai.summary: Seven tea estates in Kerala's Vandiperiyar region announced a lockout after 17 months of pending salaries and benefits, with the company citing bank loan withdrawal due to a protest by the AITUC-affiliated union.

facts.claim: Seven tea estates in Keralam’s Vandiperiyar announced a lockout
facts.quote: Deepening the crisis in the struggling tea plantation sector in the Peerumade hills in Keralam’s Idukki, seven tea estates at Vandiperiyar have announced a lockout.

facts.claim: The affected estates belong to the POABS Group
facts.quote: According to officials, the affected estates belong to the POABS Group.

facts.claim: The lockout was announced on Friday (November 13) at the Pambanar, Granby, Munjamullay (Manjumala), Nellikai, Thengakal, Injikadu, and Pasumallay (Pashumala) estates
facts.quote: The lockout was announced on Friday (November 13) at the Pambanar, Granby, Munjamullay (Manjumala), Nellikai, Thengakal, Injikadu, and Pasumallay (Pashumala) estates.

facts.claim: Spanning over 6,000 acres, the properties include Granby — one of the oldest and most historically significant tea estates in the region
facts.quote: Spanning over 6,000 acres, the properties include Granby — one of the oldest and most historically significant tea estates in the region.

facts.claim: Salaries and other benefits have been pending for the past 17 months, resulting in repeated strikes
facts.quote: According to workers, salaries and other benefits have been pending for the past 17 months, resulting in repeated strikes.

facts.claim: The POABS Group took over the seven estates in 2008 through a Provident Fund (PF) auction
facts.quote: The POABS Group took over the seven estates in 2008 through a Provident Fund (PF) auction.

facts.claim: The estates were previously owned by the RBT Group, which had abandoned them years earlier
facts.quote: The estates were previously owned by the RBT Group, which had abandoned them years earlier.

facts.claim: The POABS Group stated that repeated protests by labour organisations deepened the crisis and led to the lockout
facts.quote: The POABS Group stated that repeated protests by labour organisations deepened the crisis and led to the lockout.

facts.claim: During talks at the chief plantation officer’s office on November 12, the company agreed to announce a draft plan by November 25 to resume operations at full capacity
facts.quote: An official said that during talks at the chief plantation officer’s office on November 12, the company agreed to announce a draft plan by November 25 to resume operations at full capacity.

facts.claim: Various plantation unions attended the meeting, agreed to the decisions, and promised not to conduct any protests until November 25. However, the AITUC-affiliated High Range Employees Labour Union (HEL) staged a protest in front of the owner’s house and office in Thiruvalla
facts.quote: Various plantation unions attended the meeting, agreed to the decisions, and promised not to conduct any protests until November 25. However, the AITUC-affiliated High Range Employees Labour Union (HEL) staged a protest in front of the owner’s house and office in Thiruvalla,

facts.claim: As a result of the protest, a bank that had offered a loan to the company withdrew the offer, which resulted in the immediate announcement of the lockout. The estates were being run on bank loans, and in the present situation, the company could not secure any funding and decided to stop operations at the seven estates
